overall: Atlanta is warming under mostly clear skies (FEW clouds, 12% cloud fraction) with a running max of 77.0°F at 10:30 ET, rising at +1.8°F/hr. The day is tracking notably cooler than the NWS official forecast of 87°F, consistent with the NWP model consensus which clusters well below that figure. No tropical or severe weather threats affect Atlanta; the active flood warnings are for the Satilla River in far southeastern Georgia and are irrelevant to today's high temperature.
forecast_obs_notes: There is a striking divergence between the NWS text forecast (87°F) and the NWP model suite — ECMWF (80.7°F), NBM (80.1°F), and HRRR (83.2°F) all point to a high in the low-to-mid 80s. max_temp_prediction: With the running max at 77.0°F and ~4–6 hours of heating remaining before the modeled peak (~14.7–16.7h ET), a simple extrapolation at the current +1.8°F/hr rate (which will decelerate) yields a peak near 83–85°F. The D1_NOW distribution peaks strongly at 84–85°F (57.6%) and HRRR at 83.2°F anchor the estimate; low dewpoints (53.6°F) and clear skies support efficient solar heating, nudging the estimate toward the upper end of that range. Confidence is moderately high — the even-bucket ensemble rates this Tier 1 — with the primary downside risk being afternoon cloud development or a sea-breeze-driven wind shift that could cap heating short of 84°F.
